complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Setup React Router and Core Page Architecture
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down React Router setup into: 1) Install and configure React Router v7 with TypeScript, 2) Create AppRoutes configuration with type-safe route definitions, 3) Build RootLayout component with navigation structure, 4) Create core page components for each route, 5) Implement NotFoundPage and error boundaries, 6) Wire up navigation and verify complete routing system
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: React Router v7 introduces new data loading patterns with loaders and actions which adds complexity beyond basic routing. The file-based routing architecture, type-safe route parameters, error boundaries, and integration with the application shell require careful coordination. While routing is a well-established pattern, the v7 specifics and comprehensive page structure make this moderately complex.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Dark Mode UI Theme System
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down dark mode theme system into: 1) Configure Tailwind 4.x with zinc color palette and dark mode defaults, 2) Install and configure Shadcn UI component library via CLI, 3) Create ThemeProvider component for managing theme state, 4) Set up design tokens in tailwind configuration for consistent theming, 5) Integrate ThemeProvider and verify dark-mode-first implementation
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Implementing a dark-mode-first design system requires coordinating multiple layers: Tailwind 4.x CSS variables, Shadcn UI component library configuration, React context for theme management, and localStorage persistence. The zinc color palette customization, system preference detection, and ensuring no flash of incorrect theme add complexity. The integration of design tokens and ensuring consistency across all components requires careful planning.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Build Core Zustand State Management Architecture
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down Zustand state management into: 1) Install Zustand 5.x with middleware packages, 2) Design TypeScript interfaces for all store states, 3) Implement TimelineStore with clips, tracks, and playhead management, 4) Create MediaStore for assets and upload queue, 5) Build ProjectStore for metadata and autosave, 6) Implement EditorStore for preview and tool selection, 7) Set up store providers with React Context pattern, 8) Configure IndexedDB persistence and devtools integration
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: State management architecture is foundational and affects the entire application. Managing multiple interconnected stores (Timeline, Media, Project, Editor) with proper TypeScript typing, middleware integration (persist, devtools, immer), and IndexedDB persistence is complex. The vanilla stores with React Context pattern in Zustand 5.x requires careful implementation. Ensuring proper reactivity, avoiding unnecessary re-renders, and setting up local caching strategies adds significant complexity.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down timeline component into: 1) Install and configure react-virtuoso, 2) Build TimelineRuler with time markers and zoom controls, 3) Implement TrackList with virtualized rendering, 4) Create ClipRenderer with optimized display, 5) Implement frame-based timebase calculations, 6) Add zoom controls with keyboard shortcuts, 7) Build track type system (video/audio/text), 8) Implement horizontal scroll synchronization, 9) Add clip selection, snapping, and drag-and-drop
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: The timeline is the most complex UI component in a video editor. Virtualization of potentially hundreds of clips while maintaining smooth scrolling, synchronized ruler and track scrolling, frame-accurate timebase calculations, and responsive zoom controls is highly complex. The drag-and-drop with snapping logic, multi-track coordination, and performance optimization to handle large timelines efficiently makes this one of the most challenging frontend tasks.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Media Upload System with S3 Integration
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down media upload system into: 1) Create MediaUpload component with drag-and-drop UI, 2) Implement file validation against size/type limits, 3) Request presigned URLs from backend API, 4) Implement direct-to-S3 upload with XMLHttpRequest, 5) Build upload progress tracking system, 6) Create upload queue management in MediaStore, 7) Handle concurrent uploads with error recovery and retry logic
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Direct-to-S3 uploads with presigned URLs involve multiple steps and error-prone network operations. Managing file validation (100MB images, 1GB videos, 500MB audio), progress tracking with XMLHttpRequest, concurrent upload limits, and error recovery requires careful implementation. The integration with backend for presigned URLs, thumbnail generation requests, and upload queue state management adds complexity.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Build Playback Engine with DOM-based Preview
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down playback engine into: 1) Create PlaybackEngine class structure, 2) Implement frame ticker with requestAnimationFrame, 3) Build frame-to-clip resolver for active clips, 4) Implement video source switching for video tracks, 5) Create DOM layer system for images/text overlays, 6) Apply CSS transforms for clip properties, 7) Build playback controls UI component, 8) Implement Web Audio API for audio synchronization, 9) Add preview quality settings, 10) Optimize for sub-100ms interaction response
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Building a real-time playback engine is one of the most complex tasks in a video editor. Coordinating video playback, audio synchronization with Web Audio API, dynamic DOM layer composition, and maintaining smooth 30fps playback with requestAnimationFrame is extremely challenging. The hybrid approach of video elements with DOM overlays, frame-accurate seeking, variable playback speeds, and sub-100ms interaction response targets require sophisticated optimization and precise timing coordination.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down WebSocket system into: 1) Create WebSocketService class with connection management, 2) Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff, 3) Build heartbeat/ping-pong mechanism, 4) Create message handlers for job.update events, 5) Integrate with Zustand stores for state updates, 6) Implement connection status indicator UI, 7) Handle authentication and session management, 8) Add message queuing for offline scenarios
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Real-time WebSocket communication requires handling complex network scenarios including disconnections, reconnections, and message ordering. The integration with job lifecycle (queued, running, succeeded, failed, canceled), state management updates, authentication, and graceful degradation when offline adds significant complexity. Exponential backoff, heartbeat mechanisms, and typed message interfaces require careful implementation.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Export System with FFmpeg Pipeline
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down export system into: 1) Create ExportModal component with all settings inputs, 2) Implement export settings validation, 3) Build composition data serialization for backend, 4) Create POST request to /api/v1/compositions/, 5) Implement WebSocket listener for export progress, 6) Build progress visualization UI, 7) Handle export completion with download functionality and error states
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: The export system involves complex coordination between UI, backend API, and WebSocket updates. Managing export settings (aspect ratio, resolution, format, quality, frame rate), validating combinations, tracking progress through WebSocket events, and handling various error states requires careful implementation. The integration with job queue visualization and download URL handling adds moderate complexity.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Build AI Generation Interface for Images and Videos
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down AI generation interface into: 1) Create AIGenerationPanel UI component, 2) Build prompt input and quality tier selection, 3) Implement image generation flow with Nano-Banana API, 4) Implement video generation flow with Wan Video I2V API, 5) Create generation queue with concurrency limits, 6) Add generated assets to media library and implement generation history
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: While AI generation involves external API integration and async job management, the patterns are similar to the export system. The complexity comes from managing two different generation types (images and videos), quality tiers, aspect ratio selection, and MAX_GENERATIONS concurrency limits. The WebSocket integration and media library insertion are well-established patterns, making this moderately complex.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement Clip Editing Features and Transitions
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down clip editing features into: 1) Implement trim handles with drag in/out points, 2) Create split at playhead functionality, 3) Build clip duplication and deletion operations, 4) Implement transform controls (opacity, scale, position, rotation), 5) Create transition system (fade, cross dissolve, wipes), 6) Build clip properties panel with inline editing, 7) Add keyboard shortcuts for common operations, 8) Integrate undo/redo system with Zustand middleware
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Clip editing operations require precise calculations, intuitive UI interactions, and seamless integration with the timeline state. Transform controls with visual handles, maintaining aspect ratio locks, and proper position calculations add complexity. The transition system needs to affect both the timeline representation and playback preview. Implementing a robust undo/redo system with Zustand middleware that properly captures and restores state for all operations is challenging.
